title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of Family Trial Methods and Work Mechanisms (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Further Deepening the Reform of Family Trial Methods and Working Mechanisms (For Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2018] No. 12

To all High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to implement the people-centered philosophy, promote the reform of family trial work, and give full play to the role of family trial functions, the Supreme People's Court has, since June 1, 2016, selected some courts nationwide to carry out pilot work on the reform of family trial methods and working mechanisms. On the basis of summarizing the pilot work, the following opinions are hereby put forward on further deepening the reform of family trial methods and working mechanisms:

I. General Requirements

1. Accurately grasp the direction and goals of the reform, maintain the harmony and stability of marriage and family, protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors, women, and the elderly in accordance with the law, cultivate and practice socialist core values, promote social harmony and healthy development, and continuously meet the people's ever-growing needs for a better life and new needs and expectations for family trial work.

2. Firmly establish a humanized trial philosophy, extend the protection of the parties from identity interests and property interests to personality interests, security interests, and emotional interests, protect the privacy of the parties, pay attention to humanistic care, give full play to the role of family trials in diagnosing, repairing, and treating marital relationships, promote civilized and progressive marriage and family ethical concepts, and advance the construction of family traditions and family virtues.

3. Effectively change working methods, strengthen the judge's ex officio investigation, discretion, and appropriate intervention in the parties' right of disposition, pay attention to distinguishing between marital crises and marital death, correctly handle the relationship between protecting marriage freedom and maintaining family stability, give full play to the application of family investigation reports, psychological counseling reports, and big data, strive to objectify the criteria for adjudication and combine reason, sentiment, and law in the reasoning of judgment documents.

4. Continuously innovate working mechanisms, actively seek support from party committees and governments at all levels, strengthen coordination and cooperation with relevant functional departments and units, mobilize and encourage all sectors of society to participate, promote the establishment of a diversified dispute resolution mechanism combining judicial, administrative, and social forces, and jointly create a social governance pattern of co-construction, co-governance, and shared benefits.

5. Actively promote the professionalization of institutions and teams, establish specialized family trial institutions or teams, explore the establishment of special access mechanisms, training mechanisms, and assessment mechanisms for family judges, explore the allocation of judicial auxiliary personnel specifically engaged in family mediation, family investigation, psychological counseling, and other work, strengthen the occupational safety protection of family judges, and improve measures for the prevention and control of extreme incidents.

II. Family Mediation

6. When hearing family cases, the people's courts shall enhance mediation awareness, expand mediation methods, innovate mediation mechanisms, improve mediation capabilities, and integrate mediation throughout the entire trial process of the case. Cases that cannot be mediated due to their nature, such as those involving the validity of marriage, confirmation of status relationships, or applications for personal safety protection orders, are exceptions.

7. Rely on specially invited mediation to do a good job in mediating family cases. By assigning or entrusting specially invited mediation organizations or specially invited mediators to conduct mediation before filing a case or after filing a case in accordance with the law, the parties shall be urged to reach a mediation agreement on the basis of equal consultation to resolve the dispute. Family mediation committees may be established, conditions for registration may be set, and the procedures for specially invited mediation in the family field shall be standardized.

8. People's mediation, administrative mediation, commercial mediation, industry mediation, and other organizations with mediation functions established in accordance with the law may apply to join the roster of specially invited mediation organizations of the family mediation committee. Individuals of good character, fair and upright, enthusiastic about mediation work, and with strong communication and coordination skills may apply to join the roster of specially invited mediators of the family mediation committee.

The people's court may invite deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, people's jurors, experts and scholars, lawyers, grassroots legal service workers, arbitrators, retired legal workers, grassroots workers, and other individuals with professional knowledge in social sciences, humanities, law, education, psychology, marriage and family, etc., to join the roster of specially invited mediators of the family mediation committee. In areas where ethnic minorities live in concentrated communities, individuals familiar with local languages, customs, religious beliefs, etc., may be invited to join the roster of specially invited mediators of the family mediation committee.

9. For disputes suitable for mediation, before registration and filing, with the consent of the parties, or if the parties have not applied for mediation but the people's court deems mediation necessary, the dispute may be assigned to a specially invited mediation organization or specially invited mediator for mediation.

If the parties are severely disturbed emotionally or psychologically and cannot express their opinions normally, and the situation is urgent and requires the initiation of relevant litigation procedures as soon as possible, unless both parties apply, pre-filing assignment mediation shall not be conducted.

10. For disputes suitable for mediation, after registration and filing, the people's court may conduct mediation by itself or entrust it to a specially invited mediation organization or specially invited mediator for mediation.

11. In mediation of divorce cases, both parties shall appear in person. If a party truly cannot appear in court for mediation due to special circumstances, unless the party cannot express their will, they shall issue a written opinion.

12. The mediation process of family cases shall not be made public, unless both parties agree to make it public.

Persons presiding over mediation and participating in mediation shall keep confidential the state secrets, business secrets, personal privacy, and other information not suitable for disclosure learned during the mediation process and during the mediation process. If mediators violate the duty of confidentiality and cause damage to the parties, they shall bear corresponding legal liability.

13. During the entrusted mediation process, if the specially invited mediator deems that an investigation of factual issues is necessary, they may submit an application to the people's court. The people's court shall decide whether to entrust a family investigator to conduct the investigation based on the needs of the case.

14. Other matters concerning mediation and specially invited mediation shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Specially Invited Mediation of the People's Courts.

III. Family Investigation

15. During the trial of family cases, for matters that require further clarification, the people's court may conduct its own investigation and collection of evidence, may entrust relevant institutions to conduct investigations, or may entrust a family investigator to conduct an investigation on specific facts.

16. The people's court shall establish a roster of family investigators. The court that establishes the roster shall issue certificates to the family investigators included in the roster and manage the roster. The roster established by a higher-level court may be used by a lower-level court.

17. Family investigators shall be recommended by judicial administrative departments, education departments, the Women's Federation, the Communist Youth League, communities, and other grassroots mass organizations, and shall be selected and appointed by the people's court.

The people's court may invite deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, people's jurors, people's mediators, experts and scholars, lawyers, grassroots legal service workers, arbitrators, retired legal workers, grassroots workers, and other individuals with professional knowledge in social sciences, humanities, law, education, psychology, marriage and family, etc., to join the roster of family investigators.

18. Family investigators shall be of good character, fair and upright, enthusiastic about mass work, and have strong communication and coordination skills and rich social knowledge and experience. Individuals with grassroots work experience and a professional background suitable for handling family disputes may be given priority in selection and appointment. In areas where ethnic minorities live in concentrated communities, individuals familiar with local languages, customs, religious beliefs, etc., may be given priority for selection.

19. In a specific case, there shall be no fewer than two family investigators, selected by the people's court from the roster. After the people's court selects the family investigators, it shall notify the parties within three days. If a party has an objection to the family investigator with justifiable reasons, or if both parties jointly select another family investigator, the people's court shall select and confirm another one.

20. If a family investigator falls under any of the following circumstances, the party has the right to apply for withdrawal:

(1) The investigator is a close relative of a party or their agent;

(2) The investigator has an interest in the dispute;

(3) The investigator has other relationships with the party or agent that may affect a fair investigation.

If the family investigator falls under the above circumstances, they shall withdraw on their own, unless both parties agree to the investigation by that investigator.

The withdrawal of a family investigator shall be decided by the people's court.

21. Based on the needs of the case trial, the people's court may entrust a family investigator to investigate the following matters:

(1) The personal experience, personality, educational level, physical and mental condition, family situation, marital relationship, living environment, work situation, etc., of the parties;

(2) The situation of child-rearing, the psychological condition and learning status of the children, etc.;

(3) The situation of support for the elderly, etc.;

(4) Other matters that need to be investigated.

22. A family investigator may conduct investigations in the following ways:

(1) Conduct face-to-face interviews and exchanges with the parties themselves and their parents, children, or other relevant persons, and observe the relationship between the parties and their children, parents, or other relevant persons;

(2) Solicit the wishes and attitudes of children over eight years of age regarding custody and visitation matters;

(3) Visit the community where the parties reside, their work units, the children's schools, etc.;

(4) Other investigation methods.

23. For each investigation matter, the investigation shall be conducted jointly by two or more family investigators. The family investigator shall complete the investigation work within 15 days from the date of entrustment by the people's court and submit a written investigation report to the people's court. If it is truly difficult to complete the investigation matters within the above period, an extension may be applied for to the people's court, but the maximum extension shall not exceed 30 days. The investigation report shall include all matters entrusted by the people's court for investigation, and may include the analysis and suggestions of the family investigator.

24. After receiving the family investigation report, the people's court shall inform the parties of the content of the family investigation report and allow the parties to state their opinions.

The family investigation report may be used as a reference by the people's court in trying the case.

25. If the family investigator learns during the investigation that the parties have domestic violence, harm the legitimate rights and interests of minors, or other circumstances, they shall promptly report to the people's court and may also report to other relevant functional departments or relief agencies.

26. Family investigators have a duty of confidentiality regarding business secrets or personal privacy learned during the investigation. If a family investigator violates the duty of confidentiality and causes damage to the parties, they shall bear corresponding legal liability.

27. Family investigators shall not engage in the following acts:

(1) Soliciting business during the investigation process;

(2) Charging fees from the parties;

(3) Accepting requests from the parties or accepting improper benefits;

(4) Other acts of improperly performing duties and harming the legitimate rights and interests of the parties.

If a party discovers the existence of the above circumstances, they may file a complaint with the people's court. If verified upon review, the people's court shall immediately stop the investigation work, not adopt the submitted investigation report, and depending on the circumstances, issue warnings, circulate a notice, remove from the roster, or take other corresponding measures.

IV. Psychological Counseling

28. Under any of the following circumstances, the people's court may, based on the actual situation, recommend that the parties or minors involved in the case receive psychological counseling:

(1) One party agrees to divorce, while the other party does not agree to divorce and is emotionally agitated;

(2) In cases involving visitation disputes, custody disputes, and other disputes related to parent-child relationships, the parties have significant emotional fluctuations;

(3) There is domestic violence that has caused a significant impact on the physical and mental health of the parties;

(4) The minor involved in the case has significant emotional fluctuations or abnormal behavior and requires psychological counseling;

(5) Other circumstances where psychological counseling is necessary.

29. The people's court may establish a collaborative mechanism with relevant local government agencies or relevant psychological organization institutions or psychological education research institutions for providing psychological counseling to the parties or minors in family cases.

The specific form and content of the collaborative mechanism shall be determined through consultation between the people's court and the relevant institutions and organizations.

30. The people's court is responsible for screening cases that require psychological counseling intervention and initiating the psychological counseling process.

The collaborative institution is responsible for selecting psychological counselors to implement the psychological counseling work.

31. If the people's court, upon review, finds that a party or minor involved in the case needs psychological counseling, it may propose psychological counseling to the party or the guardian of the minor. If the party or the guardian of the minor agrees to receive psychological counseling, they shall fill out a "Confirmation of Consent to Receive Psychological Counseling." The party may also voluntarily apply to receive psychological counseling and submit a "Application for Psychological Counseling."

The people's court shall, within three days after receiving the "Confirmation of Consent to Receive Psychological Counseling" or the "Application for Psychological Counseling," issue a "Letter of Contact for Psychological Counseling Work" to the collaborative institution. Within three days after receiving a reply from the collaborative institution indicating consent, the people's court shall negotiate with the party and the collaborative institution to determine the time and place for psychological counseling.

32. During the process of psychological counseling, if the party clearly indicates that they do not wish to continue receiving psychological counseling, the process shall be terminated, and the people's court shall note this in the case file.

33. Psychological counselors have a duty of confidentiality regarding the business secrets or personal privacy of the parties learned during the psychological counseling process. If a psychological counselor violates the duty of confidentiality and causes damage to the parties, they shall bear corresponding legal liability.

34. After the psychological counseling work is completed, the collaborative institution shall issue a psychological counseling report to the people's court, which the people's court may use as a reference for hearing the case. The relevant materials of the psychological counseling shall be filed in the subsidiary case file and shall not be disclosed to the public.

V. Trial Rules

35. Before court session, the people's court shall inform the parties of their general litigation rights and obligations, the principles for allocating the burden of proof, the right to apply for investigation and evidence collection, the issuance of personal safety protection orders, legal aid, and reduction or exemption of litigation costs.

36. For family cases involving personal privacy, the people's court shall not hear them in public.

For family cases involving minors, if a public hearing is not conducive to protecting the interests of the minors, the people's court shall not hear them in public.

In divorce cases, before the court session, the people's court shall ask the parties whether they apply for a non-public hearing. If a party applies for non-public hearing, the court may not hear it in public.

For other family cases, if a party applies for non-public hearing, and the people's court, upon review, finds that it is not appropriate to hear the case in public, the court may not hear it in public.

37. In cases involving confirmation of status relationships and divorce cases, unless the person cannot express their will, the parties shall appear in court in person to participate in the litigation. If the party is a person without civil capacity, their legal representative shall appear in court. If it is truly impossible to appear in court due to special circumstances, the party must submit a written opinion to the people's court and entrust a litigation agent to appear in court to participate in the litigation.

If a party who should appear in court to participate in the litigation fails to appear without justifiable reasons after being summoned by subpoena, if they are the plaintiff, it may be treated as a withdrawal of the lawsuit in accordance with Article 143 of the Civil Procedure Law; if they are the defendant, a default judgment may be made in accordance with Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law.

If the legal representative of a party without civil capacity fails to appear without justifiable reasons after being summoned by subpoena, the above provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis. When necessary, the people's court may issue a warrant to compel their appearance.

Parties, witnesses, and expert witnesses who are truly unable to appear in court due to special circumstances may, with the permission of the people's court, participate in court sessions and other litigation activities through audio or video transmission.

38. When hearing a family case involving the determination of child custody, the people's court shall fully listen to the opinions of children over eight years of age. When necessary, the people's court may separately inquire about the opinions of minor children and provide an inquiry environment that meets the psychological characteristics of minors.

39. When hearing a divorce case, the people's court shall handle the issues of child support and property division together. If it is truly inappropriate to handle the property division issue together, the parties may be informed to file a separate lawsuit.

If the parties do not raise claims regarding child support or property division in a divorce lawsuit, the people's court shall explain to the parties and guide them to clarify their claims. If the parties fail to reach an agreement on child support and insist on not requesting the people's court to handle the child support issue, the court may rule against the divorce.

40. When hearing a divorce case, with the consent of both parties, the people's court may set a cooling-off period of not more than three months.

During the cooling-off period, the people's court may conduct mediation, family investigation, psychological counseling, and other work based on the circumstances of the case. After the cooling-off period ends, the people's court shall notify both parties.

41. In divorce cases decided by judgment or mediation, upon the application of the parties, the people's court may issue a divorce certificate to the parties.

42. In cases involving minors, such as custody disputes, visitation disputes, and child support disputes, regarding facts related to the protection of the interests of minors, the people's court shall investigate and collect evidence upon the application of the parties or ex officio.

43. In divorce cases, regarding facts such as the property status of the parties, if it is difficult for the parties to provide evidence and it affects the outcome of the case, the people's court shall investigate and collect evidence from relevant financial institutions, the parties' work units, and other relevant institutions based on the parties' application and the clear clues provided.

If the parties admit facts related to the confirmation of status relationships or public interests, in the absence of other evidence, such admission generally cannot be used alone as the basis for deciding the case.

44. In divorce dispute cases involving property division issues, when serving the notice of case acceptance and the notice of response to the lawsuit, the people's court shall simultaneously serve the "Property Declaration Form for Parties in Family Cases."

The parties shall fill out the "Property Declaration Form for Parties in Family Cases" before the expiration of the period for providing evidence, comprehensively and accurately declaring the relevant status of the community property and personal property.

The people's court shall clearly inform the parties of the legal consequences of failing to declare property truthfully. For parties who refuse to declare or intentionally fail to declare property truthfully, in addition to possibly giving them a smaller share or no share of the community property when dividing it in accordance with the law, the people's court may also give them a reprimand; if the circumstances are serious, the matter may be recorded in the social credit system or the professional integrity record; if it constitutes obstruction of civil proceedings, compulsory measures such as fines and detention may be taken.

45. If a party applies to the people's court for a personal safety protection order, they shall provide evidence that they have suffered domestic violence or are at risk of domestic violence. If the people's court, upon review, finds that there is a risk of domestic violence, it shall promptly issue a personal safety protection order.

VI. Team Building

46. Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts may, within the prescribed total number of internal institutions, establish family trial business institutions by adding a nameplate or setting up a separate institution. If conditions are not met, a specialized collegial panel or trial team may be established within the relevant trial division to be responsible for hearing family cases.

47. Judges hearing family cases, in addition to legal knowledge, shall also possess certain knowledge of sociology, pedagogy, and psychology.

The composition of a family trial collegial panel shall include at least one female judge or one female people's juror.

People's courts shall periodically provide training in trial practice, mediation skills, psychology, and other relevant areas to judges, judge assistants, court clerks, and people's assessors engaged in the trial of family cases, thereby strengthening the judicial capacity of family case trial personnel.

48. People's courts may equip judges with judicial support personnel such as specially invited mediators, family investigators, and psychology professionals to assist in the trial of family cases.

People's courts may, in conjunction with the Women's Federation, judicial administration departments, health departments, and other relevant bodies, periodically organize training for judicial support personnel and conduct assessments.

49. People's courts shall, based on actual circumstances, provide compensation for lost work, transportation, and other expenses to specially invited mediators and family investigators, and grant material or honorary rewards to specially invited mediation organizations, specially invited mediators, and family investigators who have demonstrated outstanding performance.

When people's courts engage psychological counselors to carry out relevant work, they shall pay appropriate remuneration.

The funds for the above-mentioned compensation or remuneration shall be included in the special budget of the people's court. People's courts may, in accordance with relevant regulations, apply to relevant departments for special funds.

July 18, 2018
